subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Hi Jordan & Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Attendees: Jordan (Product), Priya (AI Eng), Marissa (AE), Rishi (SE), Dev (Integration).

Key pain points you shared:
- High latency and cost for on-demand question-answering over your knowledge base (peak usage during support hours).
- Need deterministic structured outputs for downstream analytics (not just freeform text).
- Concern about embedding freshness and reranking quality for user-facing search.

Goals:
1) Reduce median token latency from ~400ms to <200ms for interactive search.
2) Produce JSON-structured responses (intent, entities, confidence) for analytics and routing.
3) Improve retrieval quality via embeddings + reranking while keeping embedding refresh within nightly job.

Product fit notes / integration considerations we discussed:
- SDK changes: lightweight client library with built-in streaming and function-calling helpers; we recommend using Redwood's structured outputs to enforce a JSON schema for answers.
- Streaming: we can stream partial responses to the UI to hit interactive SLAs; SDK supports chunked streaming and error/resume behavior.
- Function calling: Redwood supports typed function-calls; we can map detected intents to internal service calls (sample mapping attached).
- Embeddings & reranking: recommend nightly embedding refresh for updated docs + an in-memory ANN for low-latency kNN; use Redwood reranking endpoint post-retrieval for final ordering.

Technical asks from Acme:
- Sample dataset (anonymized) or a small doc dump to prototype embedding tuning.
- Expected concurrency/peak qps during support hours.
- Any strict data residency or retention constraints.

Next steps / ownership:
- Rishi will schedule a 60-min technical deep dive to walk through SDK examples and a small PoC plan (proposed Tuesday 2/16).
- Priya to share a sample doc set by EOD Wed (2/16) or confirm if you want us to work with a redacted set.
- Marissa (me) to follow up with an initial statement of work and a pricing band for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Attachments: redwood-integration-mvp-plan.xlsx (high-level PoC tasks & milestones), redwood-security-overview.pdf (SOC2, data controls).

If anything above is off, flag it — otherwise we’ll run with the plan and Rishi will send a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — couple of technical notes and quick answers to Priya’s questions.

Data residency / retention:
- Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured to keep all data in a US region and enforce 90d retention with automated deletion policies. We’ll include retention settings in the PoC config.

Embedding latency & infra strategy:
- For ~2M 768-dim vectors we recommend:
  * Quantized embeddings (8-bit) stored in-memory on a host with ~128GB RAM dedicated to ANN serving.
  * Use HNSW with tuned ef/construction for low p95. In our benchmarks, with a 2M index on optimized infra we hit p95 retrieval ~25–45ms depending on ef_search and k.
  * Add a lightweight post-retrieval reranker endpoint on GPU (or batched CPU) that takes top-N candidates and reranks with a cross-encoder. That step typically adds ~10–25ms p95 if batched properly.

SDK / integration notes:
- SDK changes: we’ll provide a sample client with:
  1) streamingResponse() helper that returns an event stream you can pipe into the frontend; handles partial JSON assembly and resume-on-error.
  2) functionCall() wrapper that maps detected schema to a typed RPC call signature in your codebase.
  3) structuredOutput(schema) validator that enforces JSON schema and returns parsing errors with token offsets for debugging.

- Function calling / structured outputs: we propose shipping a small schema for Support-Reply payloads (intent, entities, suggested_action, confidence). The SDK will support fallback strategies if required fields are missing.

- Embeddings / reranking tuning: Rishi suggests a PoC with 3 experiments: baseline retrieval-only, retrieval + lightweight dot-product rerank, retrieval + cross-encoder rerank. We can instrument quality via a small eval set you provide.

Estimated effort & timeline:
- PoC (prototype index + reranker + streaming demo): 3–4 weeks (SE-led, part-time)
- Technical deep-dive: 60 mins to walk through the sample SDK and an initial architecture diagram — I’ll send the invite for Tue 2/16 10am PT.

Action items for Acme:
- Priya: share redacted dataset (or a 5k sample)
- Jordan: share expected peak qps and internal SLOs

I’ve attached a quick draft architecture sketch and the SDK checklist. If you want, Dev and I can stand up a short-lived PoC environment under a dev account.

—Rishi
